item.title: Explicit resonance and bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays
item.description: arXiv:2611.13031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays. For general multiple-delay systems with a quadratic potential, we establish a Hamiltonian formulation with a \(P_{n,m}\)-boundary condition and derive explicit Maslov index and nullity formulas. For the special case of two distributed delays, we extend the analysis to general nonlinear potentials. These results yield explicit resonance criteria, bifurcation conditions, and Rabinowitz type and Fadell-Rabinowitz type alternatives for $\mathbb{R} $-distinct solutions.
item.dc:creator: Huiting He, Chungen Liu

item.title: Effect of car-centric social norms on traffic congestion in a compartmental model of transit mode utilization
item.description: arXiv:2611.13265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vehicle traffic congestion is a persistent feature of urban transportation systems around the world.Importantly, congestion is in part a consequence of human decision-making: car traffic is reduced when people choose modes of transportation such as metro trains, buses, or trams, over cars, and it is amplified when there is a persistent social bias towards driving. The underlying feedback loop in which traffic levels influence transportation mode choices, which in turn affect traffic levels themselves, is poorly understood and we study its consequences in the presented work using a compartmental modeling approach. We first consider a simplified model of only car traffic and show that it predicts a hysteresis between congested and uncongested states, which is consistent with broader literature on on traffic modeling. Next, we add buses and trains to the model as alternative transit modes, confirm the existence of hysteresis in this generalization, and derive the relative trip completion rates of each mode. Finally, to account for decision-making, we take the demand rates for the different transit modes to be dynamic, closing the feedback loop between mode choice and utilization. This redistributes demand for each mode of transportation, highlighting that traffic conditions may be a key aspect of mode choice. Furthermore, our model predicts that increasing public awareness of congestion can be an effective control strategy to increase utilization of public transit. However, car-centric social norms must be sufficiently small, or car use is instead amplified.
item.dc:creator: Alia Valentine, Anastasia Bizyaeva

item.title: From oscillations to symmetry breaking in a two-dimensional piecewise-smooth dynamical system
item.description: arXiv:2611.13318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a discrete-time dynamical model in which two players, each distributed over two positions, interact only at the positions of their maximal presence, with an intensity set by an external resource. The main idea is that the evolution of the maxima closes into a self-contained two-dimensional piecewise-smooth map that can be analysed exactly. We show that a single critical level of the resource separates two outcomes: below it, the players exchange leadership forever along a stable cycle; above it, the symmetry between them breaks, and an arbitrarily small initial advantage grows into a permanent winner--loser hierarchy. The local stability of these regimes is proved, and their global attractivity is supported by numerical experiments. At the critical level itself, all dominance is erased and both players end in equal division of the resource. Mathematically, the transition is a border-collision bifurcation shaped by this symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Oksana R. Satur

item.title: Local Periodic Orbit Penetration in Dynamical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.13416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce two complementary frameworks for studying local periodicity and recurrence in dynamical systems. In the topological setting, we consider continuous maps with nonempty periodic-point sets, restricted to the closures of their periodic points. We define the periodic penetration time of an open set as the least period of a periodic point it contains. Using dynamically refined finite generating covers, we construct asymptotic mean and variance invariants that describe local periodic penetration relative to the logarithms of minimum subcover cardinalities. We establish their invariance under topological conjugacy and investigate their behavior for finite periodic systems, full shifts, shifts of finite type, and zero-entropy systems with dense periodic points. We also extend the construction to invertible systems using symmetric dynamical refinements. In the measure theoretic setting, we define local return times through positive measure intersections of measurable sets with their iterated preimages. Using dynamically refined finite generating partitions, we construct corresponding asymptotic mean and variance invariants and establish their invariance under measure-theoretic isomorphism. We derive explicit formulas for finite probability-preserving systems and study finite periodic approximations of uniform Bernoulli shifts on $q\geq 2$ symbols, proving that their system-level mean and variance invariants converge to $1/\log q$ and $0$, respectively. Our results demonstrate that local periodic penetration and return-time statistics provide information about dynamical systems beyond that captured by classical entropy.
item.dc:creator: Diyath Nelaka Pannipitiya

item.title: Minimal dynamics with polynomial and intermediate complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.13420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how complicated the orbits of a minimal system can be when the topological entropy vanishes, by looking at the exact order of growth of the number of distinguishable orbit segments, and not only at its exponent. For a broad class of growth rates, including all polynomial ones, we construct minimal homeomorphisms of one-dimensional continua realizing them; in particular, two such systems may have the same polynomial entropy and yet incomparable growth. We also show that passing from a minimal subshift to the maps obtained by running its suspension flow for a fixed time only rescales time in the growth law, and we characterize exactly when this rescaling has no effect. Combined with a construction of Cassaigne, this yields minimal homeomorphisms of continua whose growth lies strictly between all polynomial and all exponential rates.
item.dc:creator: Heric Corr\^ea, Gabriel Lacerda

item.title: Fractional-Order Hybrid SIR Forecasting of COVID-19 in Bangladesh and the United States: Memory Effects and Out-of-Sample Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2611.13590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional-order epidemic models are often justified by memory, yet whether memory improves forecasts is rarely tested out of sample. We extend a hybrid SIR framework, in which a daily transmission rate is reconstructed from reported cases and then forecast, to Caputo fractional order $\alpha\in(0,1]$. We prove well-posedness, conservation, positivity and a linearized threshold at disease-free states, and derive a Gr\"unwald-Letnikov reconstruction that reduces exactly to the integer-order one at $\alpha=1$. Our main theoretical result shows that for $\alpha<1$ the influence of the unknown initial infectious count vanishes, but no faster than $t^{-\alpha}$; after 332 daily steps it is about $4.4\times10^{8}$ times larger at $\alpha=0.9$ than at $\alpha=1$. In out-of-sample forecasting over 27 weekly origins, the effect of memory depends on the setting. In Bangladesh the integer order gives the lowest error for linear and constant-rate forecasts in 47 of 48 settings. In the United States, where reported cases reached about 18% of the population, a fractional order lowers the linear forecaster's error in all 12 comparisons in 2021 but raises the constant-rate forecaster's, with no difference significant after Holm adjustment. Against standard baselines, the SIR-based linear forecaster was more accurate than the classical SIR model and a neural network without SIR structure, and competitive with ARIMA: in the United States the fractional linear forecaster had the lowest error of all methods (seven-day MAPE 7.54% against 9.14% for ARIMA), whereas in Bangladesh ARIMA had the lowest MAPE, with no significant difference from ARIMA in either country. The choice of a fractional order should rest on out-of-sample evidence rather than in-sample fit.
item.dc:creator: Md Babul Hossain, Mohammad Shah Alam

item.title: Unstable Entropy and Volume Growth for Partially Hyperbolic Diffeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.13682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a $C^{1}$ diffeomorphism on a compact manifold $M$ admitting a partially hyperbolic splitting $TM=E^{cs}\oplus E^{u}$ where $E^{u}$ is uniformly expanding. We establish a lower bound for the unstable topological entropy (w.r.t. $E^{u}$): $$h^{u}_{\rm top}\left(f\right)\geq\limsup_{n\to+\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log\int_{M}\left|\det \left(Df^{n}_{x}|_{E^{u}}\right)\right|\,dx.$$ Moreover, if there exists a measure of maximal unstable entropy whose Lyapunov exponents along $E^{cs}$ are all non-positive, then equality holds and the $\limsup$ is in fact a limit.
item.dc:creator: Yuntao Zang

item.title: Berry phase and Hannay angle as Taylor coefficients of the minimal action
item.description: arXiv:2611.13702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom whose parameters are varied slowly around a closed loop, with slowness $\delta$, we study the minimal action $\beta_\delta$ of the resulting time-periodic system and its convex conjugate, Mather's $\alpha$-function $\alpha_\delta$, both normalized per unit time. The cycle map of such a system is an area-preserving map of the cylinder which in general is not integrable. We prove that $\beta_\delta(\rho)$ and $\alpha_\delta(c)$ have asymptotic expansions in $\delta$ to every finite order, locally uniformly in the rotational regime of the frozen systems, and we identify the coefficients geometrically. The zeroth coefficient of $\alpha_\delta$ is the average of the frozen effective Hamiltonians, as shown by Evans and Gomes. The first coefficient is the classical Berry phase: at fixed rotation number $\rho$, the first Taylor coefficient of $\beta_\delta(\rho)$ is, modulo periods, Weinstein's Berry phase of the loop of frozen invariant curves of the class whose averaged frozen frequency is $\rho$, each curve weighted by its Mather measure. In particular, the minimal action selects the weighting in Weinstein's construction. The Hannay angle, the derivative of the Berry phase, governs the rotation numbers of all minimizing measures, including those supported on Aubry--Mather sets of the cycle map, where no invariant curve exists; and the intervals of classes on which a rotation number is locked have length $O(\delta^\infty)$. Since the expansions concern exact convex functions, no adiabatic approximation is involved. A transformation rule under loops of point transformations explains why the Berry phase is defined only modulo $2\pi c\mathbb{Z}$. Linear oscillators, treated by the same method, recover Berry's formula for the generalized harmonic oscillator and show that the expansions are asymptotic only.
item.dc:creator: Karl Friedrich Siburg

item.title: Limit theorems for dispersing billiards with infinite cusps
item.description: arXiv:2611.13786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extending Lenci's work in CMP (2002), Chaos (2003), we present new insights into semi-dispersing billiards with infinite cusps. We investigate the Convergence to Stable Processes (CSP) and Functional Central Limit Theorems (FCLT) both for the collision map and for the billiard flow. Whereas the billiard map always preserves an infinite measure equivalent to Lebesgue, the billiard flow preserves the Lebesgue measure, which is either finite or infinite depending on the finiteness of the area of the billiard table. When the reference measure is infinite, the usual LLN fails, but we are able to prove the CSP and FCLT. We also prove classical FCLT for the flow when the area of the billiard table is finite. These results are obtained through a precise study of the properties of the billiard map, combined with a general approach based on induction and on coupling involving point processes.
item.dc:creator: Marco Lenci, Fran\c{c}oise P\`ene, Hong-Kun Zhang

item.title: On funnel control with star-shaped funnels
item.description: arXiv:2611.13824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Funnel control for the trivial control-affine prototype is extended to the case of star-shaped funnels, both in the special case that the dynamical system is formulated in an Euclidean space and the general case of a Riemannian manifold.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Kirchhoff

item.title: From Complex Regularization to Polynomial Flow: Capture and Escape in Rocking Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.13861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a planar polynomial system based on a complex regularization of free rocking and analyze the equilibrium states and phase portraits via an effective radial potential. The conflict between the centrifugal effect, which is introduced by means of regularization, and gravity yields a potential well and an escape barrier for 0 < beta < 27/256; both vanish at a saddle-node bifurcation point. The exact energy conservation law allows us to separate dissipative relaxation, conservative periodic motions along the radial direction, and energy creating trajectories. The node-focus boundary of finite equilibria is different from the degeneracy condition for compactification at infinity. As the last step of analysis, we reconstruct the complex phase portrait and discover that a stable radial equilibrium corresponds to a relative equilibrium in the regularized dynamics, whereas the reconstruction of an impact dynamics requires taking a singular limit.
item.dc:creator: Francisco Prieto-Castrillo, Set P\'erez-Gonz\'alez, Jes\'us S. P\'erez del R\'io

item.title: Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.13904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ denote, respectively, the sets of Borel and $\sigma$-invariant probabilities on the uncountable set $\Omega=\{1,2,...,d\}^\mathbb{N}$. Given a H\"older Jacobian $J$, the dual Ruelle operator $\mu \in \mathcal{M} \mapsto \mathcal{L}_{J}^* (\mu)$ will play the role of a dynamical channel; generalizes the action of a stochastic matrix on probability vectors. Since $\mathcal{L}_{J}^*$ generally breaks $\sigma$-invariance, we introduce the \emph{ni-entropy} $h_{ni}(\mu)$ for non-invariant measures, employing the concept of the expected value function on cylinders of size one. $h_{ni}(\mu)$ differs from Shannon entropy but extends the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy from $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ to $\mathcal{M}$; $h_{ni}$ is concave and u.s.c. This leads us to the concept of ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}(A)$ of a potential $A:\Omega \to \mathbb{R}$. $\mu\in \mathcal{M}$ is not a density with respect to a dominating measure. We define an {\it ni-Kullback-Leibler divergence} $D_{ni}(\rho || \nu)$ not assuming absolute continuity. We investigate concepts of Information Theory such as Minimal Output Entropy, Donsker-Varadhan variational principle, a variational formula for $h_{ni}$, bounds for divergence, information projections, and their connections to the ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}$.
item.dc:creator: Artur O. Lopes, Elismar R. Oliveira

item.title: Frege's election method: discrepancy, invariant polygons and Farey geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.13996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a comprehensive study of Frege's modified election method as a proportional allocation rule and as a dynamical system. The method was introduced by Harrenstein, Lackner and Lackner (2022) as a modification of Frege's original proposal (1918), and it coincides with the greedy algorithm for the chairman assignment problem studied by Coppersmith et al. (2011). We consider several aspects of this method. First, we prove that the harmonic bound on the discrepancy earlier shown to be sharp for time-dependent vote proportions remains sharp for fixed vote proportions; we further quantify the restrictions on votes needed for the discrepancy to come close to this bound. Secondly, the method defines a dynamical system with a piecewise translation which, for almost every vote vector, has a unique compact attractor made up of finitely many polytopes, and every orbit is equidistributed on it, whatever choices are made at ties. Thirdly, for three parties, the dynamics is two-dimensional. We construct the invariant polygons explicitly and give a complete description of the geometry governing their bifurcations as the votes vary in the two-dimensional parameter space; this space is partitioned into a countably infinite number of ``Farey cells'' indexed by reduced fractions in $(0,\frac12]$, and each of them is further partitioned into a finite number of stability domains, separated by stability walls. In an open Farey cell indexed by a reduced fraction $u/v$, the invariant polygon has $4v+3$ vertices inside each stability domain and $4v+2$ on an internal stability wall. We construct the Farey cells explicitly and determine all stability walls and their endpoints; we also show that stability walls in different Farey cells combine to form a pattern of triangles.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Pierre Conze, Svante Janson, Anders \"Oberg

item.title: Quasi-equatorial controlled switching in inertial magnetization dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.14069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We design exponentially decaying transverse magnetic fields for reliable and ultra-fast (picosecond) magnetization reversal governed by the inertial Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation. The control construction uses an explicitly resolvable auxiliary model to select the field amplitude and characterize the influence of its decay rate, with the aim of obtaining reversal followed by relaxation without requiring a precisely timed interruption of the excitation. The auxiliary model is obtained through an equatorial approximation, and bounds on its latitude identify a regime consistent with quasi-equatorial motion. For the full nonlinear macrospin dynamics, an energy argument accounting for both inertial kinetic energy and the remaining field input provides a sufficient condition excluding backhopping, even while the exponential tail remains applied. Approximate confinement times and optimal decay rates are derived from the competition between field decay and inertial relaxation. Numerical simulations confirm the usefulness of these design estimates and identify their limitations near a capture boundary, where nearby pulses can lead to opposite final states. Spatially resolved inertial micromagnetic simulations further support reversal followed by relaxation over the simulated interval and quantify the transient departures from spatially coherent motion. The resulting approach combines explicit pulse design with a full-system energy certificate, while distinguishing rapid initial rotation from safe confinement and subsequent relaxation.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Fortunati, Massimiliano d'Aquino

item.title: On ergodicity and symmetry for affine systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.14187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a volume-preserving affine diffeomorphism of a compact homogeneous space with smooth centralizer ${\mathcal Z}^{\infty}(f)$. We establish the following two equivalences: (1) $f$ is ergodic if and only if ${\mathcal Z}^{\infty}(f)$ is a finite-dimensional Lie group; (2) $f$ is non-ergodic if and only if ${\mathcal Z}^{\infty}(f)$ contains either $C_c^{\infty}((0,1),\mathbb{R})$ or $\mathrm{Diff}_c^{\infty}((0,1))$. This strengthens the corresponding perturbative version established in arXiv:2504.09084. We also prove analogues of the above equivalences for affine-induced diffeomorphisms on bi-homogeneous spaces, frame flows over negatively curved manifolds, and automorphisms of Kummer-type complex surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Danijela Damjanovic, Amie Wilkinson, Chengyang Wu, Disheng Xu

item.title: Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions along vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2608.22514v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate diffusion approximations for a class of multivariate inhomogeneous finite-velocity random motions motivated by models of active particles. A particle alternates cyclically among prescribed velocity fields $V_1,\dots,V_p$ with random run times and evolves according to either a \emph{flight} dynamics, consisting of piecewise-linear motion, or a \emph{gliding} dynamics, in which the particle follows the corresponding velocity flow. Under a Kac-type scaling that couples vanishing run times with diverging particle speed, we prove weak convergence of both processes to multidimensional diffusions. It turns out that the order of successive cyclic motions affects the diffusion limit. In addition to the second-order term generated by fluctuations of the random run times, the limiting drift contains directional derivatives $DV_i[V_j]$ of the underlying vector fields. In Stratonovich form, part of this drift is expressed through their Lie brackets $[V_i,V_j]$. Thus, the generic non-commutativity of the microscopic motions survives the diffusive scaling and generates a macroscopic drift which depends on the cyclic order. The limiting drift also distinguishes the flight and gliding dynamics, despite their being driven by the same vector fields and run times. Several examples, including run-and-reverse motion and cyclic dynamics generated by multiple vector fields, illustrate how the cyclic switching protocol and the geometry of the underlying velocity fields shape the limiting diffusions.
item.dc:creator: Olga Aryasova, Ilya Pavlyukevich, Yusif Sualah

item.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
item.description: arXiv:2610.41635v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion on extended phase space for nonconservative and/or nonautonomous dynamical systems, with particular attention given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. Time reparameterization is also considered, clarifying when it does or does not preserve Hamiltonian structure. The analytical mechanics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates; the main developments are not predicated on a Lagrangian description.
item.dc:creator: Joseph T. A Peterson, Manoranjan Majji, John L. Junkins

item.title: Oscillations in two-stage contagion on networks: contagion structure, turnover and connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.12920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two-stage contagion describes processes, such as the adoption of an opinion or of a technological novelty, in which an individual must be exposed to an adopter twice before adopting. With demographic turnover these processes can generate waves of adoption and abandonment. We study these oscillations in a two-stage contagion model with turnover through a reservoir of inactive individuals and a small rate of spontaneous activation, and report four main findings. (i) In the mean-field description the oscillations are born at a supercritical Hopf bifurcation and require a predominantly two-stage contagion (first-contact adoption probability $Q\lesssim0.17$) and a slow turnover; spontaneous activation acts as a perturbation that destroys them. (ii) In finite populations demographic noise sustains quasi-cycles also outside this region, with a spectrum and variance predicted by a linear noise approximation away from the Hopf bifurcation. (iii) Reducing the connectivity of the network damps the oscillation, because naive nodes see fewer active neighbours than in a well-mixed population, and correlations measured in simulations confirm this damping mechanism; a pair approximation predicts that the sustained cycle disappears below a critical mean degree $\kc$, which decreases as $Q$ and the turnover rate decrease, and a finite-size test with up to $3.2\times10^5$ nodes confirms this threshold in simulations. (iv) At low connectivity the amplitude no longer depends on $Q$, so that sparsity erases the signature of the two-stage mechanism, whereas a faster turnover reduces the relative amplitude at every connectivity. The irregular dynamics observed in simulations are noise-driven quasi-cycles, not chaos.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no, Luca Meacci, Mario Primicerio

item.title: A novel derivative-corrected within-host viral model based on Caputo-Fabrizio fractional dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.12929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study an implicit within-host viral dynamics model for uninfected target cells $H(t)$, infected cells $I(t)$, viral load $V(t)$, and damaged or removed cells $D(t)$. The model contains a parameter $\mathfrak{a}\in[0,1]$ that blends the classical instantaneous within-host dynamics with derivative-dependent correction terms. We rewrite the system as an explicit ordinary differential equation whenever a computable determinant $\Delta(H,V)$ is nonzero, derive sufficient conditions for local and global well-posedness, prove positivity and conservation of $H+I+D$, compute the basic reproduction number by the next-generation approach, and analyze long-time behavior. Under natural nondegeneracy assumptions, $I(t)\to0$, $V(t)\to0$, $H(t)\to H_\infty>0$, and $D(t)\to D_\infty$. We also derive peak conditions, a final-size identity, and discuss the biological interpretation of $\mathfrak{a}$ as a dynamical responsiveness or short-memory parameter.
item.dc:creator: Dora Sele\v{s}i, Danijela Rajter-\'Ciri\'c, N\'ora Juh\'asz, Gergely R\"ost

item.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.12931v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(\Lambda)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $\Lambda$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(\Lambda)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $\Lambda$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.
item.dc:creator: Shantanu Sardar

item.title: Quadratic Bendixson criterion for delay systems: a numerical implementation
item.description: arXiv:2611.12972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a software implementation (as a Python package) of approximation schemes for verifying frequency inequalities arising from the quadratic Bendixson criterion for systems of delay equations (with a single delay in the linear part). In applications to dissipative nonlinear autonomous systems, such inequalities ensure global stability. The theoretical foundations of this approach were developed in our related work. In particular, it was shown that the transfer operators involved into the frequency inequalities can be represented as integral operators with bounded kernels of the Hardy--Volterra type. Here, we use this representation to construct approximation schemes based on finite-dimensional truncations of the transfer operators. Examples of using the package are provided.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Anikushin, Andrey Romanov

item.title: The Supercritical Ten Martini Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.13068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We solve the ten martini problem for the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum of any nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schr\"odinger operator. The proof uses the intrinsic symplectic structure of the dual center of Ge--Jitomirskaya [28] and extends the Kotani--almost-reducibility strategy of Ge--Jitomirskaya--You [30] from two-dimensional centers to arbitrary finite center dimension.
item.dc:creator: Lingrui Ge, Svetlana Jitomirskaya, Jiangong You

item.title: Smooth actions of Baumslag-Solitar groups on the interval
item.description: arXiv:2611.13171v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study representations of the Baumslag-Solitar group $BS(m,n)=\langle a,b\mid ab^ma^{-1}=b^n\rangle$ inside the group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of the interval $[0,1]$. We prove that for integers $n,m\in \mathbb Z\setminus\{-1,0,1\}$, the group $BS(m,n)$ embeds into $\mathrm{Diff}_+^1([0,1])$ if and only if $|n|=|m|$. Furthermore, we show that for any $\alpha\in (0,1)$, the group $BS(m,n)$ embeds inside $\mathrm{Diff}_+^{1+\alpha}([0,1])$ if and only if $1=|m|=|n|$ or when $1=m\leq n$.
item.dc:creator: Franco G\'omez, Crist\'obal Rivas

item.title: Pulsatile Endocrine Regulation with a Releasable Hormone Pool: Impulsive Feedback Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.13277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An impulsive model of endocrine regulation equipped with frequency- and amplitude-modulated pulsatile feedback is extended to study the dynamical effects pertaining to limitations due to the releasable hormone pool. The model describes a three-hormone regulatory loop and is applicable to endocrine systems such as the reproductive, stress, and growth hormone axes. Conditions guaranteeing the existence and uniqueness of a periodic solution with a single feedback-triggered impulse per period (a 1-cycle) are derived, together with monotonicity properties of its characteristics. An explicit Jacobian formula is obtained to assess local orbital stability. Model analysis demonstrates that a reduced hormone-pool replenishment rate produces a lower-amplitude, higher-frequency 1-cycle. This behavior is consistent with experimentally observed alterations in testosterone regulation in aging human males.
item.dc:creator: Anton V. Proskurnikov, Alexander Medvedev

item.title: Quantifying the impact of 3D diffusion and local versus global removal by surface deposition on indoor airborne transmission
item.description: arXiv:2611.13372v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS) [Xue et al. 2024] combines architectural layout, people movement, and airborne transmission modelling to predict infection risk in indoor spaces. The modelling assumptions in VIRIS include: (i) uniform aerosol concentration over the building height, allowing airborne transmission to be modelled in a two-dimensional (2D) domain, and (ii) first-order global removal of aerosols to account for surface deposition. Both assumptions lead to underestimating the infectious aerosol concentration in the breathing zone. Here, we extend VIRIS to model airborne transmission more realistically and compare the impact on infection risk predictions. We develop VIRIS-3D-L by extending the airborne transmission model in VIRIS (a reaction-diffusion equation) to three dimensions (3D) and replacing global removal with a Robin boundary condition representing localised removal due to surface deposition. We compare VIRIS and VIRIS-3D-L across three single-storey buildings with increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home, and a supermarket. We find that VIRIS underestimates the disease transmission rate and infection risks for individuals by up to 50% relative to VIRIS-3D-L in all three buildings. However, VIRIS-3D-L requires, on average, four times the computation time of VIRIS, mainly because it extends the computational domain from a 2D surface to a 3D volume. Overall, VIRIS-3D-L provides a more realistic modelling of airborne transmission than VIRIS and is particularly suited to settings with variations in people and furniture heights and frequent 3D movement. For simpler single-storey buildings, VIRIS is suitable because of its lower computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Neha Bansal, Katerina Kaouri, Thomas E. Woolley

item.title: Towards funnel control on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.13838v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Funnel control for time-invariant control-affine systems with relative degree one is transferred to the case of dynamical systems evolving on a Riemannian manifold. It is shown that, under some regularity assumptions, the classical proofs carry over. The regularity assumptions reflect the particularities of the nonlinear theory and degenerate in the classical Euclidean case.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Kirchhoff, Thomas Berger

item.title: Energy Dissipation Along Trajectories and Wasserstein Gradient Flow of Aggregation-Diffusion Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we established the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations on bounded domains involving both nonlinear diffusion and nonlocal interaction effects. Our approach is based on stochastic analysis. More precisely, we investigated the associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) with normal reflection at the boundary from a trajectorial perspective and derived a semimartingale decomposition of the corresponding energy process. This decomposition leads to a trajectorial energy dissipation identity, which, together with the characterization of the metric derivative, allows us to establish the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of the aggregation-diffusion equation.
item.dc:creator: Honglei Chen, Xuewei Wang

item.title: Decay rates for monotone operator flows in the space of probability measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.14078v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the mean-field dynamics of large populations of interacting agents, we study the long-time behavior of flows driven by monotone demicontinuous operators on the Wasserstein space. For cocoercive operators, we prove that the flow converges to a zero of the operator and that the operator residual and the metric speed decay as $o(t^{-1/2})$, so that the population comes to rest (the agents asymptotically stop moving). We also consider Tikhonov regularized flows of merely monotone demicontinuous operators and show that the operator residual and the metric speed tend to zero, with rate $O(1/t)$ when the Tikhonov parameter is $\alpha/t$ with $\alpha\geq 1$, and that the trajectory converges to the zero of minimal second moment, which is a Dirac mass, so that the agents reach consensus (all agents reach the same point). Finally, we study a discrete analogue for nonexpansive operators and show that the generated sequence converges to the fixed point closest to a reference Dirac mass; this fixed point is again a Dirac mass, so that consensus is also reached under this scheme. The main arguments rely on a specially tailored superposition principle, which represents the flow as a curve in a fixed Hilbert space of random trajectories, where the crucial estimates are derived.
item.dc:creator: Radu Ioan Bo\c{t}, Alberto Dom\'inguez Corella, Tr\'{\i} Minh L\^e

item.title: Invariant measures, Gelfand pairs and integral representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that whenever a Gelfand pair acts cocompactly on a locally compact space, there is a measure relatively invariant under a "parabolic" subgroup. That result seems new even for simple Lie groups, in which case it admits a much more direct proof. Along the way, we obtain for general Gelfand pairs a variant of Furstenberg's invariant ray theorem for minimal parabolics. We use this to establish an integral representation theorem for positive spherical functions in complete generality, extending the Harish-Chandra representation. A similar representation theorem is given for positive harmonic functions.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Monod

item.title: Long-time behaviour of solutions for equations with randomness
item.description: arXiv:2611.14396v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We discuss results on the mixing properties of solutions for discrete and continuous time equations, drived by stationary bounded random forces, obtained during the last three years in a number or our joint papers. To facilitate applications of these results to specific equations with randomness, the results are edited and properly re-arranged.
item.dc:creator: Sergei Kuksin

item.title: Newton non-degenerate holomorphic foliations and their separatrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.14466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study germs of holomorphic foliations in the complex plane that are Newton non-degenerate. This is an algebraic condition attached to the Newton polygon of the foliation, analogous to the one defined by Kouchnirenko for analytic curves and, more generally, hypersurfaces. As in this case, the condition of Newton non-degeneracy for foliations can be identified through the comparison of two numerical invariants: the Newton number - a computation involving simple geometric data of the Newton polygon - and the Milnor number. The Newton number is never greater than the Milnor number, and the foliation is Newton non-degenerate if and only if they are equal. The assumption that a foliation is Newton non-degenerate imposes conditions on its set of separatrices. We prove that, under this hypothesis, the foliation has no weak separatrices and, hence, all its separatrices are analytic. We also give a description of the set of separatrices of a Newton non-degenerate foliation, which is sufficient to characterize the foliation as Newton non-degenerate when it is of generalized curve type. This allows us to prove that the property of being Newton non-degenerate is topologically invariant for foliations of generalized curve type.
item.dc:creator: Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, Evelia R. Garc\'{i}a Barroso, Rog\'erio Mol

item.title: Herman's converse KAM mechanism revisited
item.description: arXiv:2512.03313v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In his counterexample to the KAM theorem, Herman used a hyperbolic perturbation together with a bump and asked whether the latter was necessary \cite[p.~78, Remark~4.7.3]{H1}. Motivated by this question, we compare destruction and persistence for a sine perturbation, with and without a Gevrey bump. The combined perturbation destroys all invariant circles with sufficiently small nonzero rotation numbers, whereas the sine perturbation alone preserves a sequence of analytic invariant circles in the same frequency range.
item.dc:creator: Yi Liu, Lin Wang

item.title: A Dynamical Fekete-Szeg\H{o} Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2603.01684v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a compact set, symmetric with respect to the real axis and regular for the Dirichlet problem. A classical theorem of Fekete and Szeg\H{o} asserts that if $cap(E)\ge 1$ then every neighbourhood of $E$ contains infinitely many complete sets of conjugate algebraic integers. We prove a dynamical strengthening: $cap(E)\ge1$ if and only if every neighbourhood of the polynomially convex hull $Pc(E)$ contains filled Julia sets of monic integral polynomials of arbitrarily large degree. When $cap(E)=1$, we show that the minimal polynomials $P_n$ of distinct algebraic integers whose entire Galois orbits approach $E$ have filled Julia sets $K_{P_n}$ converging to $Pc(E)$ in the Klimek metric, and Brolin measures converging to the equilibrium measure $\mu_E$. The key step is that algebraic numbers of small Rumely height $h_E$ have minimal polynomials that are asymptotically minimal on $E$. As an arithmetic application, we show that the Call--Silverman canonical heights $\hat{h}_{P_n}$ converge to $h_E$ uniformly on $\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$.
item.dc:creator: Turgay Bayraktar, Melike Efe

item.title: Computing Families of Periodic Solutions of the 4- and 6-Body Problems Using an Adaptive Gradient-Free Stochastic Method
item.description: arXiv:2604.05653v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we numerically compute planar periodic motions of the 4- and 6-body problems. We consider a 4-body configuration formed by two opposite pairs of bodies and a 6-body configuration formed by two equilateral triangles. More generally, for two regular $k$-gons with masses $1$ and $m_2$ in the respective groups, we derive a system of four second-order differential equations for two radial and two angular variables; for $k=2$, the groups are opposite pairs. With $r_1(0)=1$, the periodicity conditions lead to an overdetermined nonlinear system consisting of eight return equations in five unknowns. We show that, for collision-free solutions, four symmetry conditions at $H=T/2$ imply these eight equations. For prescribed mass ratio and angular advance, we solve the resulting four equations in four unknowns using Newton's method. An adaptive stochastic black-box procedure, which uses only function evaluations, provides initial approximations. The method searches for solutions by sampling in an anisotropic box whose dimensions adapt using information from previous successful iterations. Exact satisfaction of the return conditions gives a motion that repeats up to rotation and relabeling; an angular advance that is a rational multiple of $2\pi$ then gives a periodic motion. We report numerical examples and check the return residuals of the printed initial conditions using both the reduced equations and independent integrations of the full Cartesian equations.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Perdomo

item.title: Existence of the Lyapunov exponent for $S$-unimodal maps
item.description: arXiv:2607.04187v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we show that for any $S$-unimodal map $T$ on $[0,1]$ with a non-flat critical point the Lyapunov exponent exists for Lebesgue almost every point and is equal to a constant $\lambda_T$. Moreover, $\lambda_T=0$ if and only if $T$ admits neither an absolutely continuous $T$-invariant probability measure with positive entropy nor a strictly stable periodic orbit. Consequently, if an $S$-unimodal map with a non-flat critical point is infinitely renormalizable or non-statistical then for Lebesgue almost every $x\in [0,1]$ the Lyapunov exponent along the orbit of $x$ exists and is equal to $0$. A key ingredient is the following result of independent interest. If an $S$-unimodal map with a non-flat critical point has no periodic attractor then for Lebesgue almost every $x\in [0,1]$ the lower Lyapunov exponent along the orbit of $x$ is non-negative. This shows that, in the absence of periodic attractors, exponential contraction cannot occur along the orbit of Lebesgue almost every point.
item.dc:creator: Yuya Arima

item.title: Proof of the singularity conjecture for discrete subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$
item.description: arXiv:2609.17506v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mu$ be a finitely supported probability measure on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ whose support generates a Zariski-dense discrete subgroup. We prove that its stationary probability measure on $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{R})$ is singular with respect to the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$-invariant probability measure. The proof compares winding variances on finite covers of a closed hyperbolic surface and uses a topological obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Timoth\'ee B\'enard

item.title: On normal forms and first integrals of planar maps at elliptic fixed points
item.description: arXiv:2609.21417v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study real-analytic planar maps, that admit a real-analytic first integral with a non-degenerate extremum, in a neighbourhood of an elliptic fixed point. We prove that, if the map preserves an analytic area form, it is real-analytically and symplectically conjugate to a twist map, both in the resonant and in the non-resonant case. Using an example, we show that without the area-preservation assumption the conclusion fails. We then prove that a second, continuous, first integral is either a function of the first one or forces the map to be periodic, in which case the map is analytically (and, when area-preserving, symplectically) conjugate to its linear part. We illustrate our results, we study the McMillan map, and a planar map obtained from the Adler--Yamilov Yang--Baxter map.
item.dc:creator: Stavros Anastassiou

item.title: Global straightening of solution manifolds for state-dependent delay equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01482v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $U$ be an arbitrary open subset of $C^1([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuously differentiable. Suppose that each derivative $Df(\phi)$, $\phi\in U$, admits a continuous linear extension $D_ef(\phi):C([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)\to\mathbb R^n$, such that $D_ef(\phi)\chi$ depends jointly continuously on $\phi\in U$ and $\chi\in C([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$. We construct a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $U$ onto an open subset of $C^1([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$ which maps the solution manifold of $x'(t)=f(x_t)$ onto an open subset of the closed subspace defined by $\phi'(0)=0$. This resolves an open problem posed by Walther concerning regularization of the entire solution manifold. The diffeomorphism preserves the value at zero and agrees with the original history on $[-h,-\tau]$ for any prescribed $\tau\in(0,h)$, and is uniformly arbitrarily close to the identity in the supremum norm. It is connected to the identity by a jointly $C^1$ family of diffeomorphisms. The same conclusions hold under the weaker assumption that the finite signed measures representing the derivatives of $f$ have no atom at zero. We also establish a corresponding theorem for separable real Hilbert-valued histories.
item.dc:creator: Lily DiPaulo

item.title: Wandering continua, renormalization, and Lebesgue measure on Julia sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.05949v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sullivan's celebrated no-wandering-domain theorem asserts that rational maps have no wandering Fatou components. In this paper, we establish a measure-theoretic counterpart for the Julia set: every wandering continuum in the Julia set of a finite-type entire function has zero area. For infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials, we also prove that almost every point in the renormalization core (the intersection of the orbits of little Julia sets) is recurrent and contained in the postcritical set. The main tool is a conservativity theorem: if $f$ is injective on a forward invariant measurable subset $E$ of the Julia set, then $f|_E$ is conservative and almost every point of $E$ is recurrent and contained in the postsingular set.
item.dc:creator: Willie Rush Lim

item.title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
item.description: arXiv:2611.08002v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.
item.dc:creator: H\'ector Barge, J. J. S\'anchez-Gabites

item.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.08353v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations, but no chaos, in Katriel's differential equations. From the elementary reactions, without reference to the differential equations, we derive a deterministic map $F_\tau$ for a large population updated in rounds of length $\tau$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. Katriel's equations are recovered as $\tau\to0$. Taking the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, with rates and round length fixed, the map goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $\beta/\gamma=46$, $\mu/\gamma=0.002$, $\gamma\tau=5.5$ the window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis beyond a subcritical Neimark--Sacker point. Chaos is supported by independent indicators: a positive Lyapunov exponent with Kaplan--Yorke dimension $1.81$, a matching correlation dimension, the 0-1 test ($K\approx1$ exactly in the window), a broadband spectrum, ordinal-pattern complexity, sensitive dependence on initial conditions and dense saddle periodic orbits. One-stage contagion, $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos. In the same window Katriel's equations have a periodic relaxation cycle: the round structure turns this oscillation into chaos and shrinks the oscillatory range in $p$ from $(0.022,0.41)$ to $(0.022,0.056)$. The chaos is thus a property of two-stage contagion with synchronous updating, not an artefact of discretisation.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no, Luca Meacci

item.title: Impulse Response Estimation via Laguerre-Fourier Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2608.14769v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The empirical transfer function estimate (ETFE) is a widely used method for system identification of linear time-invariant (LTI) systems in engineering disciplines such as acoustics, audio engineering, seismography, and tomography. However, ETFE suffers from numerical limitations when the excitation signal is band-limited or vanishes at certain frequencies, which is a common physical constraint of the excitation in practice. In such cases, division in the frequency domain becomes heavily ill-conditioned, and small measurement disturbances or numerical inaccuracies can degrade the solution. This paper presents L-ETFE, a generalization of ETFE based on Laguerre-Fourier expansions that addresses these limitations. After a suitable transformation, the method can yield a well-conditioned circulant problem even when the original ETFE system is ill-conditioned. Solving this problem via classical ETFE yields the discrete Laguerre-Fourier coefficients of the system's transfer function. The desired impulse response (IR) of the system-to-be-identified can then be recovered by a subsequent transformation pipeline. We derive novel and efficient algorithms for performing these transformations and analyse the conditioning of the transformed problem, explicitly characterizing its dependence on the input and a parameter used in the Laguerre-Fourier expansion. We evaluate the method on two simulated discrete-time LTI systems of varying complexity. The experiments demonstrate accurate IR recovery for spectral-zero and band-limited excitation, where standard ETFE fails.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as D\'ozsa, Art J. R. Pelling, Matthias Voigt

item.title: Effective Joint Equidistribution of Subspaces of Bounded Height in Rigid Adelic Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.30608v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove effective joint equidistribution for subspaces of fixed dimension in a fixed rigid adelic space over a number field. The joint distribution records the rescaled height, the archimedean position, and the shapes of the subspace and its quotient. More generally, we obtain counting estimates for regions in which the height bound may depend on the position and both shapes. Under a H\"older-type bound for the measure of boundary layers, the estimates have explicit power-saving error terms. We apply these results to counting problems involving slopes, freeness, and semistability, and to Diophantine approximation with prescribed shapes.
item.dc:creator: Ruida Di

item.title: Mechanism-Aware Ensemble Conditioning for Data-Limited Emulation of Extreme Events
item.description: arXiv:2609.30746v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Extreme events in chaotic systems are difficult to learn from short trajectories because they are controlled by finite-time instabilities rather than by frequently observed bulk dynamics. We propose a mechanism-aware conditioning plug-in framework that turns a nudged ensemble of an imperfect model into a non-intrusive sensor of the local instability geometry. In the small-noise regime, the ensemble covariance has the same finite-time deformation kernels that govern local instability, providing a Jacobian-free proxy for local amplifications around a trajectory. A small Feature-Wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) network injects the ensemble geometry into an otherwise unchanged backbone without modifying the low-fidelity model simulator. We demonstrate this interface in two settings: a Transformer-style residual-attention corrector for a controlled low-dimensional chaotic system and a probabilistic recurrent STORN corrector for topographic two-layer quasi-geostrophic (QG) flow. In the low-dimensional benchmark, leading ensemble-covariance directions identify transient instabilities that are also detected by Optimally Time-Dependent (OTD) modes. FiLM conditioning improves 99th-percentile exceedance-frequency errors over an otherwise identical unconditioned Transformer. In QG, an ensemble-conditioned FiLM-STORN model substantially improves long-horizon rare-event statistics in the data-limited regime, including density-tail errors, exceedance frequencies, and spatial exceedance-area distributions relative to an unconditioned STORN trained on the same data. On averaged high-threshold exceedance diagnostics, it also outperforms the unconditioned baseline STORN trained with 20 times more expensive trajectory data. These results show that local instability geometry is not merely interpretable post hoc, but an actionable conditioning signal for data-efficient rare-event emulation.
item.dc:creator: Isabella S. Thiel, Juan Bello-Rivas, Yannis G. Kevrekidis, Themistoklis P. Sapsis
